assumptions.obligation: Resets are asserted together: when i_rst_n_mst falls (global clock), i_rst_n_slv is low in the same step; mst reset is never asserted alone
Resets are asserted together: when i_rst_n_slv falls (global clock), i_rst_n_mst is low in the same step; slv reset is never asserted alone
i_rst_n_mst is released synchronously to i_clk_mst: it rises only in the same global step as a rising edge of i_clk_mst
i_rst_n_slv is released synchronously to i_clk_slv: it rises only in the same global step as a rising edge of i_clk_slv
The requester keeps i_apb_psel low while either reset is asserted; no transfer starts before both resets are released
After the one-cycle Setup phase the requester holds PSEL and PENABLE high until the PREADY cycle; no new Setup before PREADY
APB5 only: once i_apb_pwakeup is high in a cycle with i_apb_psel, it stays high until o_apb_pready

notes:
I rewrote the reset rules on the formal global clock. This addresses the triage findings for CHK-003, -006, -013, -014, -016 and -017. In every one of those traces, one reset is pulled low by itself, or a reset is released when its own clock has no rising edge. The specification forbids both: AB2-3-39, AB2-3-41 and AB2-6.3-27.

- **New ENV-01 and ENV-02:** these replace the old versions, which only checked the resets at clock edges. When either reset goes low, the other reset must be low in the same time step. Release may still be staggered, as AB2-7.2-11 allows. The old ENV-01 was also too strict. It could force i_rst_n_slv to stay in reset until the next i_clk_mst edge, which would rule out a legal early release in the slv domain.
- **New ENV-06 and ENV-07:** each reset can only be released in the same step as a rising edge of its own clock. Flops clocked on that edge still see the reset as active, so the release is clean.
- **Removed helpers:** r_env_rst_n_*_q is no longer needed, so I removed it.

**What I deliberately did not assume:**
1. **No clock-liveness bound.** The clocks can run at any ratio and phase (AB2-3-32), and a stopped clock can't let a reset go anyway under ENV-06 and ENV-07. AB2-20.2-02 asks for a running clock while a request is in flight, but that is a liveness requirement that a safety check doesn't need.
2. **No "requester fields stay stable during Access" rule (AB2-6.3-06).** The bridge must ignore changes during Access and use the values from the Setup cycle (AB2-6.3-25, AB2-12-06, AB2-15.1-03), so that case has to stay legal input.
3. **No "PSTRB low in a read" rule (AB2-6.3-11).** The bridge is required to pass PSTRB through unchecked (AB2-3-19, AB2-6.3-12). Assuming it would hide forwarding bugs.
4. **No rule for the "PWAKEUP glitch-free" wording.** It isn't a sequence the checker can test.

Next step: re-run the six checks with these rules. If one still fails with legal resets, it points to a real bug in the design (the triage notes name mst.sv:165-168/215 and slv.sv:163-166/215-220). The triage also suggested making the disable iff in CHK-013/014/016/017 cover both resets. That change is in the checker files, not in this environment, so it isn't part of this file.
